clue.text: Store for soldiers — and airmen too, it follows

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of British army soldiers
POs are pilot officers, junior RAF airmen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A depot set aside for army troops, with room for the air force as a logical consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it follows' sounds like a conclusion, but IT simply comes after the soldiers and airmen; 'for', 'and', 'too' and 'follows' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposit is to put something away for safe keeping, which is a synonym of the verb to store.

clue.text: Phoning or going round?

definitions.meaning: ... also means encircling, forming a ring around

explanation.surface: Making a call, or doing the rounds?
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing is telephoning someone, and also surrounding something like a ring.

clue.text: Coppers like a period for recreation

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated p
as means like
a time is a period

explanation.surface: Police officers enjoying a spell of leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police; it means copper coins, pence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a hobby or leisure activity, something done for recreation.

clue.text: Oriental inn some Japanese raided

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller's lodge in the East attacked by Japanese troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is a caravanserai, a lodging for travellers in Asia.

clue.text: Highly implausible stories!

parts.note: highly hints at height, so the stories are lofty as well as far-fetched

explanation.definitionFit: Unbelievable yarns are called by an idiom using an adjective of height.

clue.text: Shows opposition to sisters getting involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone objects to their sisters meddling in their affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting involved' rearranges the letters of SISTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to stand against it, a direct synonym of opposing it.

clue.text: Ran a small account into debit

indicators.note: into puts the account abbreviation inside the word for debit

parts.note: being in the red means being in debit
a/c, written AC, is a short form of account

explanation.surface: Someone ran a little account into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals a container; 'in the red' is the everyday idiom for owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced is the past tense of race, meaning ran fast.

clue.text: Militant leaders

parts.note: the front of an armed column or campaign is pictured as a weapon's sharp tip

explanation.definitionFit: Those at the front of an attacking movement are said to form its sharp point.

clue.text: Singers, in a spin or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Vocalists either whirling round or doing something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'otherwise' rearranges A SPIN OR. 'a spin' wants to be the anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural of soprano, singers of the highest voice.

clue.text: Starts a crawler

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Starts a crawler' (7) for SERPENT: 'crawler' defines it but 'Starts a' gives none of its letters; part of the clue appears lost in OCR and no source found

clue.text: Breathing space essential for everyone

parts.note: read literally, a 'breathing space' is not a pause but a passage air goes through, and every person has one on the face

explanation.surface: A plea that everybody deserves a little rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing space' usually means a respite; here it is a literal opening in the nose for breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is an air passage, a space used in respiration that every person has.

clue.text: Jubilation about a piano being reduced in price

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for jubilation goes round the other letters

parts.note: jubilation is shown in a cheer of joy
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Delight at a piano being sold off at a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and P inside CHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marked down costs less, which is the comparative of inexpensive.

clue.text: Introduced into it, Edward may receive excellent backing

parts.note: into gives the preposition in
taken as written

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for excellent is read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
Ted is a common short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A new member is brought into the club, and Edward may be treated to a fine endorsement.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written with the letter I for the digit; 'backing' turns it round, and 'may receive' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone initiated has been formally admitted into a group or skill, i.e. introduced into it.

clue.text: Writer of review note

parts.note: to read a text is to look it over, so review gives read
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: An author of a critical notice.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade is a nineteenth-century English novelist, so he is a named example of an author.

clue.text: Land and start back in delight

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for delight

parts.note: glee is delight or joy

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Land, and begin again happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start back' looks like 'begin again'; it is the first letter of 'back', B, which goes 'in' GLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glebe is a piece of land assigned to a parish clergyman as part of the living.

clue.text: Made the first mate beam from then on

parts.note: Eve was the first wife in Genesis, made as Adam's mate
a rafter is a sloping roof beam

explanation.surface: The first officer of a ship was made to smile broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' and 'beam' suggest a ship's officer smiling; they are Eve and a roof timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever after means for all time following a given moment, as in fairy-tale endings.

clue.text: Law-breaker wanting exceptionally silent car

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the usual order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A criminal who wants an unusually quiet getaway car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges SILENT CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so one who commits it is a thief, a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Barker the rubicund stationer

parts.note: rubicund means ruddy, red-faced
one who stations or places things is a setter

explanation.surface: A red-faced shopkeeper selling paper, named Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stationer' is read as one who sets things in position, not a paper seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A red setter is an Irish gun dog, and a dog is a barker.

clue.text: Put down the newspapers to cut the long grass

indicators.note: to cut means one word slices into the other, so the newspapers go inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Lay down the papers in order to mow the overgrown lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' signals one piece slicing into the other; 'Put down' is not burial but crushing, as with dissent.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed means suppressed or crushed, as a rebellion is put down by force.

clue.text: Replacing trees to find favour

indicators.note: replacing means placing again differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Planting new trees to win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing' rearranges TREES TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon badge worn as a token, like a rosette.

clue.text: Imprisoning for writing

definitions.meaning: shutting animals or people in an enclosure
putting words on paper with a pen

explanation.surface: Locking someone up for their scribbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen is both to enclose in a pen and to write with a pen.

clue.text: The skin will turn red to some degree

indicators.note: turn means turn round, so the word red is read backwards

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: Skin will go rather red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will turn' makes DER from RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Derma is the dermis, the layer of the skin beneath the surface.

clue.text: It's normal to draw back — back outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for back goes round the other piece

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: back here means the word for draw is read in reverse

parts.note: to lug is to drag or draw along

explanation.surface: It is normal to retreat, going back out.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'back' is a reversal signal and the second is a synonym, a neat repeat that hides the container 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means usual or conforming to a standard, the same as normal.

clue.text: An entertainer, trite as can be

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters could form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer who is as hackneyed as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as can be' reads as an intensifier; 'as' is fodder and 'can be' rearranges TRITE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Boy one accompanying a girl

parts.note: a son is a boy child
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lad walking out with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a female given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Too much viewing is a mistake

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overdone
sight is the act of seeing

explanation.surface: A warning that watching too much television is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an error caused by failing to notice something, a slip.

clue.text: Daisy's neat look

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Daisy has a tidy appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' means cattle here, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye is a large white daisy of meadows.

clue.text: Beats soft footwear!

definitions.meaning: knitted coverings for the feet worn in shoes

explanation.surface: Hits out with soft slippers.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock is to punch, and socks are knitted foot coverings.

clue.text: A plant among the first fifty

indicators.note: among says the other letters go inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
1st, written IST, abbreviates first
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A specimen plant counted among the top fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals a container; 'first' is the ordinal 1st, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is a prickly flowering plant, emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Attempts to nail the French

parts.note: to tack is to nail down with small nails
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: Efforts to pin down the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a task is to undertake it, so tackles means attempts as a verb.

clue.text: Eat greedily — turn green — go inside

indicators.note: inside says the word go sits within the other letters
turn means change, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gorge yourself till you feel sick, then go indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the change of colour but is the anagram signal, and 'inside' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To engorge is to gorge or devour food voraciously.

clue.text: About to open a game book

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in tennis the server opens play with the serve

explanation.surface: About to start a match, someone books a court.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a seat or table is to book it in advance.
